Tail FX · Formulas & functions

Every formula, and the Excel that computes it

The exam is four long questions, so each one chains several of these. Every row gives the formula, when you need it, the Excel that computes it and the solver sheet that does it for you. The step chains below show how the formulas string together in the question types that come up.

Returns, data and statistics

Simple return
r = (P₁ + D − P₀) / P₀
prices given; the additional-questions workbook (Q2, Q3)Excel: =(B3-B2)/B2Solver: Data
Log (continuous) return in your notes
r = ln(P₁ / P₀)
prices given; the SET-index and option example workbooks; your notes use it for stocks and the ZRR indexExcel: =LN(B3/B2)Solver: Data⚠ LOG() is base 10 — use LN()
Change in a rate in your notes
dy = (y_t − y_t−1) / 100
spot rates or yields quoted in %Excel: =(B3-B2)/100Solver: Data⚠ forget the /100 and every bond VaR is 100× too big; a 6-month T-bill rate is also ÷2
Mean
μ̂ = Σ r / T
every μExcel: =AVERAGE(range)Solver: Data
Standard deviation
σ̂ = √[ Σ (r − μ̂)² / (T − 1) ]
every σExcel: =STDEV(range) (= STDEV.S)Solver: Data⚠ STDEVP divides by T, not T − 1
Covariance in your notes
σ_xy = Σ (x − x̄)(y − ȳ) / (n − 1) = ρ·σ_x·σ_y
off-diagonal of ΩExcel: =COVARIANCE.S(x,y) or =COVAR(x,y)*n/(n−1)Solver: Data⚠ COVAR is the POPULATION covariance (÷ n)
Correlation
ρ = σ_xy / (σ_x·σ_y)
given σ's and ρ, or checking dataExcel: =CORREL(x,y)Solver: Data
Ω from σ's and ρ's in your notes
Ω_ii = σ_i² ; Ω_ij = ρ_ij·σ_i·σ_j
"daily volatilities … correlation …"Excel: =ρ*σi*σjSolver: Asset VaR
Annualise in your notes
μ_year = μ_day × n ; σ_year = σ_day × √n (n = 252)
daily data → yearly σ for Black-ScholesExcel: =STDEV(r)*SQRT(252)Solver: Data⚠ σ for Black-Scholes comes from PRICE returns, not rate changes
t-test of H₀: μ = 0
t = μ̂·√T / σ̂ , df = T − 1
"is the mean significantly different from zero?"Excel: =TINV(0.05,df) · =TDIST(ABS(t),df,2)Solver: Normal VaR⚠ the slide and SET-index workbook use T − 2
Skewness, kurtosis
SKEW = asymmetry ; KURT = excess kurtosis (normal = 0)
fat tails make a normal VaR too smallExcel: =SKEW(range) · =KURT(range)Solver: Data

VaR and ES of one return

VaR definition in your notes
the worst loss over a horizon at a confidence level (1 − α)
any "define VaR" question⚠ reported NEGATIVE in this course
z-value
z_α = NORMSINV(α) (1% −2.326348 · 2.5% −1.959964 · 5% −1.644854 · 10% −1.281552)
every VaRExcel: =NORMSINV(0.01)Solver: Start ▸ z mode⚠ −1.96 is the 2.5% value, NOT 5%
VaR as a return in your notes
r_α = μ + z_α·σ
μ and σ of one returnExcel: =mu+NORMSINV(a)*sdSolver: Normal VaR
VaR in money
VaR = r_α × W₀
"in Baht"Excel: =C16*W0Solver: Normal VaR
Zero-mean VaR in your notes
VaR = z_α·σ
short horizons: μ grows with T but σ with √T, so μ is negligibleExcel: =NORMSINV(a)*sdSolver: Normal VaR⚠ keep μ unless the question drops it
VaR over T periods in your notes
VaR_T = μ·T + z·σ·√T
"10-day VaR" from daily dataExcel: =mu*T+NORMSINV(a)*sd*SQRT(T)Solver: Normal VaR⚠ never multiply a VaR that includes μ by √T
Probability of a loss
P(r < X) = NORMSDIST((X − μ)/σ)
"probability of losing more than …"Excel: =NORMSDIST((X-mu)/sd)Solver: Normal VaR
Expected shortfall in your notes
ES = μ − σ·φ(z_α)/α , φ(z) = e^(−z²/2)/√(2π)
"average loss beyond the VaR"Excel: =mu-sd*EXP(-(z^2)/2)/(SQRT(2*PI())*a)Solver: Normal VaR⚠ multiplier φ/α: 2.665214 (1%), 2.337803 (2.5%), 2.062713 (5%)
Discrete VaR and ES
VaR = smallest L with P(loss ≤ L) ≥ 1 − α ; ES = average of the worst α
a few loss outcomes with probabilitiesExcel: =SMALL(losses,COUNTIF(cum,"<"&(1-α))+1)Solver: Discrete VaR-ES⚠ VaR can fail subadditivity; ES cannot
EWMA in your notes
σ²_n = λ·σ²_n−1 + (1 − λ)·u²_n−1
"λ = 0.94, update the volatility"Excel: =lam*s^2+(1-lam)*u^2Solver: EWMA⚠ u is yesterday's return; the answer is a VARIANCE until you take √
EWMA over a series
recursive: σ²_t = λσ²_t−1 + (1 − λ)u²_t−1 from σ²₁ = u₁² · weighted sum: σ² = Σ λ^(k−1)·u²_k / Σ λ^(k−1), k = 1 the latest
a column of daily returns and λ (the class EWMA workbook: 0.97)Excel: =SQRT(SUMPRODUCT(weights,u^2)/SUM(weights))Solver: EWMA⚠ the recursive σ on the last day excludes that day's return; tomorrow's includes it
Equal-weight volatility
σ = √( Σ u² / n ) (zero mean)
the class EWMA sheet's 'STDEV' lineExcel: =SQRT(SUMSQ(u)/COUNT(u))Solver: EWMA
GARCH(1,1) in your notes
σ²_n = ω + α·u²_n−1 + β·σ²_n−1 ; long-run variance = ω/(1 − α − β)
textbook context (Hull); EWMA is the case ω = 0, α = 1 − λ, β = λ
Solvency
PD = NORMSDIST((−E₀/A₀ − μ_A)/σ_A) ; capital = −(μ_A + NORMSINV(PD)·σ_A)
assets, debt, target ratingExcel: =NORMSDIST((-E0/A0-muA)/sA)Solver: Solvency

Portfolios: the matrix form

Weights
w_i = V_i / W₀
money in each assetExcel: =C11/SUM($C$11:$C$15)Solver: Asset VaR
Portfolio mean in your notes
μ_P = wᵀμ = Σ w_i·μ_i
every portfolioExcel: =SUMPRODUCT(w,mu) or =MMULT(TRANSPOSE(w),mu)Solver: every engine
Portfolio variance in your notes
σ_P² = wᵀΩw (1×n)(n×n)(n×1)
every portfolioExcel: =MMULT(MMULT(TRANSPOSE(w),Om),w) · =SUMPRODUCT(w,MMULT(Om,w))Solver: every engine⚠ Ctrl+Shift+Enter in Excel 2019 and earlier
Two assets, written out
σ_P² = w₁²σ₁² + 2w₁w₂σ₁₂ + w₂²σ₂²
hand working for two assetsSolver: Asset VaR
Portfolio VaR in your notes
VaR = μ_P + z·σ_P ; × W₀ for money
every portfolioExcel: =muP+NORMSINV(a)*sdPSolver: every engine
Individual VaR
VaR_i = (μ_i + z·σ_i) × V_i
before the diversification benefitSolver: Asset VaR
Diversification benefit in your notes
benefit = VaR_P − Σ VaR_i (> 0)
"how much does diversification reduce risk?"Solver: Asset VaR⚠ your notes: Σ individual − portfolio with VaR positive — same number
Marginal VaR in your notes
mVaR_i = μ_i + z·(Ωw)_i / σ_P ; × W₀ for money
"adding one unit of asset i changes VaR by …"Excel: =mu_i+NORMSINV(a)*MMULT(Om,w)/sdPSolver: Asset VaR⚠ (Ωw)_i is row i of Ω times w — Cov(asset i, portfolio)
Component VaR in your notes
cVaR_i = w_i × mVaR_i ; Σ cVaR_i = VaR_P
"how much of the VaR comes from asset i?"Excel: =w_i*mVaR_iSolver: Asset VaR⚠ share = cVaR_i / VaR_P
Incremental VaR
iVaR_i = VaR_P − VaR(portfolio without i)
"what if we sold asset i?"Solver: Asset VaR⚠ close to, but not equal to, component VaR

Fixed income

Zero-coupon price
B = F / (1 + y/m)ⁿ ; continuous: F·e^(−yT)
T-bill, ZCBExcel: =F/(1+y/m)^nSolver: ZCB
ZCB durations in your notes
D_mac = n ; D_mod = D_mac / (1 + y/m)
T-bill; continuous: D_mod = TExcel: =n/(1+y/m)Solver: ZCB⚠ durations are in PERIODS of the compounding
Bond return from yield change in your notes
r_B = −D_mod·dy ⇒ μ_B = −D_mod·μ_dy , σ_B = D_mod·σ_dy
every bond VaRSolver: ZCB
ZCB VaR in your notes
VaR = −D_mod·μ_dy + z·D_mod·σ_dy ; × B for money
"VaR of the T-bill"Excel: =-Dmod*AVERAGE(dy)+NORMSINV(a)*Dmod*STDEV(dy)Solver: ZCB
Coupon bond price in your notes
B = Σ CF_t / (1 + y_t)^t (each flow at its OWN spot rate)
coupon bond + spot curveExcel: =SUMPRODUCT(CF,1/(1+y)^t)Solver: Coupon Bond⚠ not one yield for all flows
PV weight in your notes
w_t = PV_t / B
coupon bond as a portfolio of zerosExcel: =G20/$G$33Solver: Coupon Bond
Macaulay and modified duration in your notes
D_mac = Σ t·w_t ; D_mod = D_mac / (1 + ytm)
"find the duration"Excel: =SUMPRODUCT(t,w) · ytm: =IRR(−B,CF₁,…,CFₙ)Solver: Coupon Bond
Adjusted weight in your notes
w_t × (−t) [formula sheet] or w_t × (−t/(1 + y_t)) [modified]
the coupon bond's exposure to each dy_tExcel: =H20*-B20Solver: Coupon Bond⚠ your notes use −D_mod; the class keys use −t (identical when discounting is continuous)
Coupon bond VaR in your notes
μ_B = Σ adj_t·μ_dy,t ; σ_B = √(adjᵀ Ω_dy adj) ; VaR = μ_B + z·σ_B
"VaR of the coupon bond"Excel: =SQRT(MMULT(MMULT(TRANSPOSE(adj),Om),adj))Solver: Coupon Bond⚠ Ω is the RAW yield-change matrix; durations live in w
Bonds + stocks in your notes
stock: multiplier 1 on its return ; ZCB: −D_mod on its rate change
mixed portfolio (additional Q2)Solver: Portfolio A⚠ weight = holding value / total portfolio value

Options

d₁, d₂ in your notes
d₁ = [ln(S/K) + (y + σ²/2)T] / (σ√T) ; d₂ = d₁ − σ√T
every Black-Scholes questionExcel: =(LN(S/K)+(y+s^2/2)*T)/(s*SQRT(T))Solver: Option BSM⚠ σ, y and T in the SAME time unit
Black-Scholes in your notes
C = S·N(d₁) − K·e^(−yT)·N(d₂) ; P = K·e^(−yT)·N(−d₂) − S·N(−d₁)
option pricesExcel: =S*NORMSDIST(d1)-K*EXP(-y*T)*NORMSDIST(d2)Solver: Option BSM
Put-call parity
C + K·e^(−yT) = P + S
check, or price one from the otherSolver: Option BSM
Delta in your notes
Δ_C = N(d₁) ; Δ_P = N(d₁) − 1 = −N(−d₁)
stock-price riskExcel: =NORMSDIST(d1)Solver: Option BSM
Rho in your notes
ρ_C = T·K·e^(−yT)·N(d₂) ; ρ_P = −T·K·e^(−yT)·N(−d₂)
interest-rate riskExcel: =T*K*EXP(-y*T)*NORMSDIST(d2)Solver: Option BSM⚠ use the actual Rho (hundreds), not a 0–1 number
Gamma, Vega, Theta
Γ = φ(d₁)/(Sσ√T) ; Vega = S√T·φ(d₁) ; Θ (class calc) = K·e^(−yT)(σφ(d₂)/(2√T) + y·N(d₂))
"all the Greeks"Excel: =EXP(-(d1^2)/2)/SQRT(2*PI())Solver: Option BSM⚠ PI(), not 22/7
Option return, Greeks method in your notes
r_Op = Δ·(S/Op)·r_S + (ρ/Op)·dy ⇒ w = [Δ·S/Op ; ρ/Op]
option VaR, approach 1Excel: =Delta*S/Op · =Rho/OpSolver: Option BSM⚠ check: w_rS − w_dy/T = 1
Working in periods
σ_period = σ_daily·√(252 × life) ; y_period = y_year × life ; T = 1
the class 3-month exercise: everything measured in 3-month periodsExcel: =SQRT(VAR(r)*252*0.25) · =y/100*0.25Solver: Option BSM ▸ build σ, y and T⚠ same prices and Delta as years with T = life; Rho and the dy weight are per unit of the period's rate
Option inside a portfolio in your notes
multiply the option's two weights by its share of the portfolio value
shares + an option (additional Q3)Solver: Portfolio B
Binomial moves in your notes
u = e^σ − 1 , d = e^(−σ) − 1 ; need d < y < u (else one asset dominates)
building block, approach 2Excel: =EXP(s)-1Solver: Option Binomial
Equivalent asset in your notes
Δ = (X₁u − X₁d)/(S(u − d)) ; B = [X₁d(1+u) − X₁u(1+d)] / [(1+y)(u − d)] ; price = ΔS + B
"construct the equivalent asset"Excel: =(Xu-Xd)/(S*(u-d))Solver: Option Binomial⚠ call = long stock + short bond (B < 0); put = short stock + long bond
Units of bonds
units = B × (1 + y)^T (face-1 zero-coupon bonds)
the equivalent asset stated in bonds, as the class binomial workbookExcel: =B*(1+y)Solver: Option Binomial
Building-block weights in your notes
w = [ΔS/Op ; −(B/Op)·T/(1+y)]
option VaR, approach 2Solver: Option Binomial⚠ the two block weights ΔS/Op and B/Op sum to 1
Numerical Greek
f′(x) ≈ [f(x + h) − f(x − h)] / (2h)
"check Delta numerically"Solver: Option BSM
Digital (cash-or-nothing)
C = e^(−yT)·N(d₂) ; Δ = e^(−yT)·φ(d₂)/(Sσ√T)
"pays 1 if …"Excel: =EXP(-y*T)*NORMSDIST(d2)Solver: Option BSM⚠ Delta uses the density φ(d₂), not N(d₂)
Delta and rho hedge
shares = −n·Δ ; ZCBs (face 1) = n·ρ / (T·e^(−yT))
"hedge the option position"Excel: =-n*DeltaSolver: Hedge

Forwards, futures and hedging

Forward = call − put in your notes
long 1 call + short 1 put at K = forward price ⇒ V_F = C − P = S − K·e^(−yT)
forward contract valueExcel: =C-PSolver: Forward
Forward weights
w_rS = S/V_F ; w_dy = T·K·e^(−yT)/V_F
forward VaRExcel: =S/VFSolver: Forward⚠ huge when V_F is small — quote the VaR in money
Cost of carry in your notes
₀F_T = S₀·e^(y_T·T)
futures on a stock or indexExcel: =S0*EXP(yT*T)Solver: Futures §1⚠ replication: borrow money, buy the stock
Futures on an asset in your notes
dFu = S₀·r_S + T·S₀·dy_T ⇒ w = [S₀ ; T·S₀]
futures VaRSolver: Futures §1⚠ weights are MONEY — a futures is worth 0 when opened
Futures on a ZCB in your notes
B₀ = X·e^(−y_T+N·(T+N)) ; ₀F_T = B₀·e^(y_T·T) ; w = [−(T+N)·B₀ ; +T·B₀]
bond futuresExcel: =X*EXP(-yTN*(T+N))Solver: Futures §2⚠ replication: borrow money, buy the ZCB
Forward rate
(T)f(N) = [y_T+N·(T+N) − y_T·T] / N
check a bond-futures priceSolver: Futures §2
Futures on a coupon bond in your notes
₀F_T = Σ X_k·e^(−y_T+k·(T+k)) × e^(y_T·T) (post-delivery flows only)
coupon-bond futuresSolver: Futures §3⚠ price must lie below the undiscounted Σ X_k; the financing row carries T
Hedge ratio (one instrument)
h* = ρ·σ_S/σ_F ; N* = h*·Q_A/Q_F
"how many futures contracts?"Excel: =rho*sS/sFSolver: Hedge §1
Best hedge with several futures
minimise (p + Hn)ᵀΩ(p + Hn) ⇒ (HᵀΩH)·n = −HᵀΩp
"minimise the risk; can it be eliminated?"Excel: =MMULT(MINVERSE(HtOH),-HtOp) or SolverSolver: Hedge §2⚠ fewer instruments than factors ⇒ a residual is left

Multi-step chains: how the formulas string together

A long exam question is one of these chains with numbers. Write the step names down first, then fill them in — the order is the marking scheme.

Portfolio of assets from money, σ and ρ"$X in A and $Y in B, daily volatilities, correlation … VaR, benefit, marginal, component"
  1. weights — w_i = V_i/W₀ Asset VaR ▸ Weights
  2. Ω — Ω_ij = ρ_ij σ_i σ_j Asset VaR ▸ Ω table
  3. μ_P and σ_P — wᵀμ ; √(wᵀΩw) Asset VaR ▸ Answers
  4. VaR, % and money — μ_P + zσ_P ; × W₀ =NORMSINV(α)
  5. T-day VaR — μ_P·T + zσ_P√T Horizon T
  6. ES — μ_P − σ_P φ(z)/α
  7. individual VaRs and the benefit — VaR_P − Σ VaR_i individual table
  8. marginal, component, incremental — μ_i + z(Ωw)_i/σ_P ; w_i × marginal ; check Σ = VaR individual table
Raw data → a mixed portfolio's VaR"the table gives eleven days of spot rates and prices; the portfolio holds ZCBs, shares (and an option)"
  1. changes — dy = Δrate/100 ; r = ΔP/P (or ln) Data ▸ paste, set 'becomes a factor via'
  2. μ and Ω — AVERAGE ; covariance matrix Data ▸ statistics, Ω
  3. price each holding — ZCB F/(1+y)^T ; option by BSM or binomial Portfolio A/B ▸ holdings
  4. value weights — value / W₀ Portfolio ▸ each holding
  5. multipliers — stock 1 ; ZCB −D_mod ; option Δ·S/Op and ρ/Op Portfolio ▸ each holding
  6. adjusted weight per factor — Σ weight × multiplier on that factor Portfolio ▸ adjusted weight per factor
  7. μ_P, σ_P, VaR — wᵀμ ; √(wᵀΩw) ; μ_P + zσ_P ; × W₀ Portfolio ▸ Answers
A coupon bond's VaR"coupon bond, spot curve, statistics of the yield changes"
  1. PV of each flow — CF_t/(1+y_t)^t Coupon Bond ▸ cash flows
  2. price and weights — B = Σ PV ; w_t = PV_t/B
  3. durations — D_mac = Σ t w_t ; D_mod = D_mac/(1+ytm) =IRR for ytm
  4. adjusted weights — w_t × (−t)
  5. μ_B, σ_B — adjᵀμ_dy ; √(adjᵀΩ adj) type μ and Ω of the dy's
  6. VaR, % and money — μ_B + zσ_B ; × B × number held Coupon Bond ▸ Answers
An option's VaR, both ways, and its hedge"call / put on a stock … VaR by the option pricing model and the building-block approach … hedge"
  1. d₁, d₂, price — BSM Option BSM ▸ price and Greeks
  2. Δ and ρ — N(d₁) ; TKe^(−yT)N(d₂)
  3. weights, check — [ΔS/Op ; ρ/Op] ; w_rS − w_dy/T = 1 Option BSM ▸ position A/B
  4. VaR (approach 1) — wᵀμ + z√(wᵀΩw) over [r_S ; dy] type μ and Ω
  5. tree: u, d, payoffs — e^σ − 1 ; e^(−σ) − 1 Option Binomial
  6. Δ, B, price, weights — equivalent asset ; [ΔS/Op ; −(B/Op)T/(1+y)] Option Binomial
  7. VaR (approach 2), compare Option Binomial ▸ Answers
  8. hedge — −nΔ shares ; nρ/(Te^(−yT)) bonds Hedge §3
Futures and forwards"price the futures … weights … VaR … forward rate … value the forward"
  1. price — cost of carry ; B₀e^(y_T T) ; ΣX_kB_k e^(y_T T) Futures §1/§2/§3
  2. check — forward rate reprices ; price < undiscounted Σ X_k
  3. weights in money — [S₀ ; TS₀] ; [−(T+N)B₀ ; TB₀]
  4. VaR in money — wᵀμ + z√(wᵀΩw) type μ and Ω
  5. forward — V_F = C − P ; [S/V_F ; TKe^(−yT)/V_F] Forward
Minimise a position's risk with futures"use the futures to minimise the bond's risk; can it be eliminated?"
  1. position exposures p — adjusted weight × value, per dy Hedge §2 (or pull from Coupon Bond)
  2. contract exposures H — −(T+N)B and +TB per futures Hedge §2 ▸ instruments
  3. solve — (HᵀΩH)n = −HᵀΩp Hedge §2 ▸ elimination
  4. risk before and after — √(pᵀΩp) → √(eᵀΩe)
  5. verdict — more factors than instruments ⇒ residual

Your handwritten notes, checked

Each line of your one-page summary against the course materials. Rows marked in your notes above come from it.

VaR = μ + z(α)·σ, z negative
Matches the course convention: VaR is reported negative and the mean is kept.
Annualise: μ × n, σ × √n; μ is negligible over short horizons
Correct, and the reason the zero-mean VaR z·σ is a fair shortcut for one or ten days. Over T periods use μT + zσ√T.
Bond rates: Δi = new − old; stocks and ZRR: ln(new/old)
Right for the example workbooks. The additional-questions workbook (Q2, Q3) uses SIMPLE returns (new/old − 1); use what the question's key uses. Rates quoted in % also need /100.
ZCB VaR = E(r) + z(D_mod × σ_Δi), E(r) = −D_mod × average(Δi)
Correct; D_mod = D_mac/(1 + YTM/m).
Coupon bond: weight × −D_mod
The formula sheet and every key use weight × (−t). −D_mod per cash flow is the modified-duration version; the two agree exactly under continuous discounting.
Diversification benefit = Σ individual VaR − portfolio VaR
Same number as VaR_P − Σ VaR_i here, because this course's VaRs are negative.
Marginal VaR = E(r)_A + z·[Ω·w]_A/σ_port; mVaR$ = portfolio size × mVaR%
Correct — the Ωw row for asset A is its covariance with the portfolio.
Component VaR$ = investment_A × mVaR_A%; ratio = cVaR_A/ΣcVaR
Correct, and the components add up to the portfolio VaR exactly.
Options: σ = stdev(Δprice) × √252, not Δinterest; interest rate of NOW
Correct and worth underlining: y is the latest spot rate, not an average.
Option weights × weight of the option in the portfolio; use the actual (big) Rho
Correct: Rho is in money per unit of rate (hundreds), and the option's weights are scaled by its portfolio share.
